newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC proposes to ease TV, radio ownership rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC proposes to ease TV, radio ownership rules.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission proposed Thursday to ease local television station ownership rules as well as rules governing the cross-ownership of radio and TV stations.

The FCC plan, which also includes a "grandfathering" policy for TV local marketing agreements, is intended to update the agency's rules in the wake of the telecommunications law passed earlier this year.
The FCC proposed to allow common ownership of TV stations that are in separate designated market areas and that do not have overlapping "Grade A" contours, or signals that extend 50 to 70 miles.
Currently, FCC rules bar a person or entity from having interests in two TV stations whose "Grade B" signal countours overlap. Grade B refers to signals that extend 30 to 45 miles.
The FCC also is seeking comment on possible exceptions and waiver criteria that would allow common ownership of two TV stations in the same local market.
In addition, it is seeking comment on whether its current restrictions on ownership of a TV and radio station in the same market are still needed, or whether the rules should be changed.

The agency has tentatively decided to waive the ban in the top 50 markets if there are at least 30 independent stations available in a market. Until now, the FCC has waived its restrictions in the top 25 markets under such circumstances.
In related matters, the FCC proposed to change the way ownership in a broadcast station is calculated when ownership involves equity or debt.

It is also seeking comment on what factors it should consider when calculating a TV station owner's national reach under the new telecommunications law provision allowing companies to own TV stations that reach 35 percent of the national audience.
Prior to the new law, companies faced a limit of 12 stations and a 25 percent audience cap.
